objective: Exploratory experiment: can the eleven-label regrowth rule (PINWHEEL-NATIVE-20261107-001A) run on the bare growing patch, the triangle T_k of one tile cut k times, with its boundary's shape as the only memory? In the unlabelled planar map of T_k, with the outer face marked by one outside vertex that the codes record but do not expand, find the least radius r at which every dart's oriented label, at the boundary and next to it included, is a function of its rooted radius-r code, at levels 4 to 7 and r up to 6. Interior darts are settled at radius 2 by ticket A; this ticket measures what the boundary adds. Controls: shuffled labels and a code that does not mark the outer face.
status: Closed, supported (exploratory, PINWHEEL-ATLAS-20261107-001D-E001): regrowth needs no labels. In the bare growing patch T_k (levels 4-7, up to 267,766 darts), every dart's oriented label, boundary darts included, is a function of its unlabelled rooted radius-2 code, pooled over all levels (3,227 codes, no conflict; radius 1 has 15 conflicts, all but one next to the boundary); marking the outer face is not even needed at radius 2. So the eleven-label rule runs on the bare patch with its shape as the only memory.
title: Regrowth with the labels dropped: does the bare patch carry its own labels?
